name: Spelljack
body:
The Spelljack is a reimagining of the spell stealing class introduced in a complete guide to adventuring from the 3.5 edition of the world’s most popular roleplaying game. One of the primary goals of this reimagining is to ensure the class has some proper versatility from level one. The spelljack has been upgraded to a caster of 6th level spells though with a much tighter spell list and also gains the ability to steal spell-like abilities at level one. Coupled with multiple options allowing a spelljack to do more than simply return a stolen spell by casting it themselves, the spelljack can now hold onto stolen magic and has several abilities that allow it to be used in new and exciting ways. From the shadow focused Blackjack to the formidable Antitheurge, we hope you find what you’re looking for and add a little bit of arcane trickery and anti caster tactics to your toolbox, as both player and GM.

Spelljacks use a combination of luck, skill, and arcane prowess to wrest power from their opponents and turn enemy magics to their will. Spelljacks are well suited to the life of an adventurer. With a robust skill set and arcane magic, spelljacks can adapt to overcome nearly any challenge, but they have neither the towering arcane might of wizards nor the brute force of barbarians. Spelljacks excel at using misdirection and deception to overcome seemingly stronger opponents, especially those who possess magic of their own.

Good spelljacks can often be found leading or organizing themselves behind noble causes, especially in ways that let them flex their many skills. Evil spelljacks are often found among thieves’ guilds, running blackmail operations, or as assassins.

Role: The spelljack is a support character typically used to thwart spellcasters.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 4d6 x 10 (140 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The spelljack’s class skills are: Acrobatics (Dex), Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Disable Device (Dex), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (Arcana), Knowledge (local) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Spellcraft (Int) Stealth (Dex), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are the class features of the spelljack.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A spelljack is proficient with all simple weapons plus the longsword, rapier, shortbow, composite shortbow, whip, and all light martial weapons.

A spelljack is proficient in light armor and shields (but not tower shields) and may cast spells in light armor without spell failure.

Detect Magic (Sp)

A spelljack must always be able to find their mark and always wary of their surroundings. At 1st level you gain the ability to cast detect magic at will with a caster level equal to your class level. Additionally, this ability allows the spelljack to detect if a creature within the spell effect has spells prepared, spell slots remaining or uses of spell-like abilities remaining.

Sneak Attack (Ex)

A spelljack takes advantage of any opening to win a fight quickly. You deal extra damage whenever an opponent is flanked by you or denied their dexterity bonus to armor class. This damage applies to ranged attacks only when made within 30ft of your target. At 1st level, this damage is 1d6 increasing by an additional 1d6 every three levels thereafter to a maximum of 7d6 at 19th level.

Trapfinding (Ex)

A spelljack adds 1/2 their level to Perception skill checks made to locate traps and to Disable Device skill checks (minimum +1). A spelljack can use Disable Device to disarm magic traps.

Steal Magic (Su)

The spelljack has learned to take magic from others and make use of it for themselves. Whenever they deal sneak attack damage to a creature they may choose to siphon some magic from the target.

When damaging a creature that has a spellcasting feature or possesses spell-like abilities, that creature must make a Fortitude save DC equal to 10 + the number of sneak attack damage dice the spelljack possesses + the spelljack’s Intelligence modifier or lose a prepared spell, spell slot, or daily use of a spell-like ability with a maximum spell level equal to the number of sneak attack damage dice the spelljack possesses. The spelljack may choose the level of the spell affected, if no spell of that level is available to lose the target loses a prepared spell, spell slot, or daily use of a spell-like ability at random of a spell level lower than the level chosen by the spelljack.

When this ability is used on a creature that spontaneously casts spells, a spelljack may choose a specific spell known, when doing so that creature loses the ability to cast the stolen spell for 1 minute. Otherwise a spell of the appropriate level is chosen at random from among spells known and that spell is unable to be cast by the target for 1 minute.

A spelljack may choose to expend the stolen magical energy to instead cast a spell they have prepared without expending the spell slot or to cast a spell they had previously prepared in the last 8 hours. In either case the spell being cast must be of an equal or lower level than the stolen magic which was spent to cast it.

A spelljack may cast a stolen spell or spell-like ability once or until the next-time they prepare spells. When casting a stolen spell calculate caster level and save DC using the spelljack’s caster level and Intelligence modifier. A spelljack may store a maximum number of stolen spells equal to the their Intelligence modifier at any given time.

When preparing spells for the day, the spelljack may choose to retain one stolen spell from those they have stored, all others are lost. A spelljack can choose to lose a stored spell as a free action or in response to stealing another spell.

A note on steal magic and related abilities:

When playing with psionics, powers are treated like spells as though using full transparency.

Any ability that references a charge of stolen magic or a spellcasting feature may be used interchangeably in regards to spells, powers and manifesting features.

Spells (Su)

A spelljack casts arcane spells drawn from the sorcerer/wizard spell list. Only spells of the abjuration, enchantment, and illusion schools appear on the spelljack spell list. A spelljack must choose and prepare their spells ahead of time.

To learn, prepare, or cast a spell, the spelljack must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a spelljack’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the spelljack’s Intelligence modifier.

A spelljack can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table: 1-2 Spelljack Spells per Day. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Intelligence score.

A spelljack may know any number of spells. They must choose and prepare their spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying their spellbook. While studying, the spelljack decides which spells to prepare.

Starting Spells: A spelljack begins play with a spellbook containing all 0-level spelljack spells plus two 1st-level spells of their choice. The spelljack also selects a number of additional 1st-level spells equal to their Intelligence modifier to add to the spellbook.

Gaining New Spells: Spelljacks perform a certain amount of spell research between adventures. Each time a character attains a new spelljack level, they gain two spells of their choice to add to their spellbook. The two free spells must be of spell levels they can cast. At any time, a spelljack can also add spells found in other spelljack or wizard spellbooks to their own or add spells to their spellbooks from scrolls in the same way a wizard can.

Cantrips (Su)

Spelljacks can prepare a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, each day, as noted on the Table 1-2: Spelljack Spells per Day. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again.

Spelljack Expertise: A spelljack learns many tricks to aid them on and off the battlefield. At 2nd level and every 3 levels thereafter, a spelljack chooses a new expertise from those listed below. Unless otherwise noted each expertise can be selected only once. If an expertise requires a saving throw the DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 the spelljack’s class level + the spelljack’s Intelligence modifier.

Battle Hardened (Ex)

The spelljack may now cast spells in medium armor and while using shields (but not tower shields) without arcane spell failure.

Better Lucky Than Good (Su)

You’ve learned to trust in luck only so much and can spend a little stolen power to bend it in your favor. Once per day when your hit points fall below 0 but not beyond a negative total equal to your constitution score, you may instead be left with 1 hit point by expending a charge of stolen magic. The spelljack must be at least 8th level before selecting this expertise.

Broadened Horizons (Ex)

The spelljack may add two spells and/or formulae to their spellbook from among the alchemist and/or sorcerer/wizard formula/spell lists. These formulae/spells must be from one of the following schools of magic: divination, evocation, or transmutation. If an archetype changes what spells are available to the spelljack, like the blackjack, you may also select one of the archetype’s qualifying spells. These additional formulae/spells must be of a level no higher than the maximum spell level the spelljack can cast and formulae added to the spellbook are prepared as spells rather than as extracts. A spelljack may select this expertise more than once.

Conduit Companion (Su)

The spelljack’s familiar now benefits from some of the spelljack’s class features. As long as the familiar is within 30 ft of its master it gains the following spelljack class features if they are also possessed by its master: spell shield, absorb magic, and reflect spell. The familiar gains the same bonus from spell shield as its master and when the familiar absorbs magic, the stolen spell is transferred to the spelljack.

Daggercloud (Su)

The spelljack has learned to make illusions more lifelike and deadly. As a full round action the spelljack can create illusory duplicates of a throwing weapon they are holding and make a full attack action, using each attack they are normally allowed in a full attack. Each attack deals only 50% damage, before applying precision damage and critical hits. These illusory doubles copy all attributes of the weapon chosen, including magical weapon qualities, and the chosen weapon is not actually thrown, only the copies. For each successful attack the spelljack deals 25% more damage to a maximum of 100%. For example if a spelljack can make 4 attacks in a full attack action, and all attacks are successful, the first attack would deal 50% damage, the second attack would deal 75% damage, the third attack would deal 100% damage and the 4th and final attack would deal 100% damage.

Additionally the spelljack gains Point-Blank Shot and Precise Shot as bonus feats usable only with thrown weapons.

Deadly Finesse (Ex)

The spelljack gains Weapon Finesse as a bonus feat without needing to meet its prerequisites. In addition, the spelljack may use their Dexterity modifier in place of their Strength modifier on damage rolls with weapons they wield which benefit from Weapon Finesse.

Disruptive (Ex)

The spelljack gains Disruptive as a bonus feat without needing to meet its prerequisites.

Drain Item (Su)

The spelljack gains the ability to steal spells from items. The spelljack may make a caster level check as a standard action (DC 10 + 2x the spell level of the spell being absorbed). If it succeeds, the item is drained and the spelljack gains the spell as if it were stolen from a spellcaster.

For single use items (like scrolls or potions), this ability uses the item as if it were used normally. If the item is charged (like wands or staves), this ability uses 5 charges from the item. If the item is a use-per-day item, it renders the spell unusable through the item for 1d6 days.

If the spelljack fails their caster level check by 10 or less, the charge or use of the spell is lost from the item but the spelljack does not gain the use of the spell.

This has no effect upon artifacts or continuous magical effects, only use-limited spells.

Familiar (Su)

The spelljack gains the service of a familiar using their spelljack level in place of their wizard level. If the spelljack already has a familiar, this expertise allows spelljack levels to stack with other character levels for the purposes of determining familiar abilities.

Guided Blade (Su)

The spelljack has a knack for finding weakness in any foe. By expending a prepared spell slot or a charge of stolen magic the spelljack may deal precision damage and critical hits to foes that would normally be immune for a number of rounds equal to the level of the spell expended.

When using this expertise the spelljack may also choose to use the higher of their Dexterity or Strength modifiers to calculate damage on their melee attacks for the duration.

Improved Familiar (Su)

The spelljack gains Improved Familiar as a bonus feat. A spell jack must have a familiar before selecting this expertise.

Improved Sneak Attack (Ex)

The spelljack’s sneak attack damage increases by + 1d6.

Interference (Su)

When doing battle with creatures animated by or composed of magic a spelljack has learned to disrupt the energies that control and power such foes. The spelljack may add precision damage on attacks against all foes of the construct, outsider and undead types even if they would be otherwise immune to precision damage. Any enemy of a type listed above which is damaged by the spelljack’s sneak attack must make a Will save or be confused for one round as the magical energy which composes and controls them is disrupted.

This confusion affects the creature regardless of any immunity to mind-affecting effects. The spelljack may spend one charge of stolen magic to instead issue a single command, as the spell, to the damaged enemy. This command does not require for the target and the spelljack to share a language and the command is not prevented by the creature’s immunity to mind-affecting effects.

Pierce Resistance (Su)

Whenever the spelljack deals sneak attack damage to a creature with any energy resistance, that creature loses an amount of energy resistance of each type they possess equal to half the spelljack’s level rounded up unless they succeed at a Will save. If a creature has an energy immunity instead replace it with resistance 30 and then apply this reduction. This reduction lasts for 1 minute.

The spelljack may expend a charge of stolen magic to increase the reduction to be equal to their character level and gain an equal amount of each resistance affected.

Pilfered Potency (Su)

Whenever a creature within 30ft of the spelljack is the target of a harmless spell or spell-like ability (even those generated by spell trigger and spell completion magic items) the spelljack may attempt a caster level check, as an immediate action, with a DC equal to 11+ the creature’s HD, if successful the spelljack steals the effect. The spelljack may expend a charge of stolen magic to extend the range of pilfered potency to 60 ft.

Poison Use (Ex)

The spelljack no longer has a chance to affect themself when applying poisons.

Additionally, they gain a bonus on Craft (alchemy) checks equal to their class level when crafting poisons.

Rend Magical Protection (Su)

Whenever the spelljack damages a foe benefitting from a deflection or resistance bonus with sneak attack, that enemy must succeed on a Will save or lose any such bonuses for a number of rounds equal to the spelljack’s Intelligence modifier. If the spelljack expends a charge of stolen magic, instead the bonuses are transferred to the spelljack for the duration. Normal stacking rules apply.

Siphon Power (Ex)

Whenever the spelljack deals sneak attack damage to a target, if that enemy has any active spell effects, such as protection from arrows, that creature must attempt a Will save.

Failure means the effect is transferred to the spelljack for 1 minute or until the effect’s duration expires. Whichever comes first. The spelljack may only steal one effect per attack that deals sneak attack damage. A spelljack must have the rend magical protection expertise before selecting siphon power.

Spellbreaker (Ex)

The spelljack gains Spellbreaker as a bonus feat without meeting its prerequisites. The spelljack must select the disruptive spelljack expertise before selecting this expertise.

Rogue Talent: A spelljack may also choose one of the following rogue talents in place of an expertise.

armor piercer, bleeding attack, canny observer, coax information, combat swipe, combat trick, honeyed words, ninja trick, scry slip.

Advanced Rogue Talent: Beginning at 11th level, a spelljack may also choose from among the following advanced rogue talents in place of an expertise:

Feat, hunter’s surprise, improved evasion, skill mastery.
Evasion (Ex)

At 3rd level, a spelljack can avoid even magical and unusual attacks with great agility. If they make a successful Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, they instead take no damage.

Evasion can be used only if the spelljack is wearing light armor or no armor. A helpless spelljack does not gain the benefit of evasion.

Spell Shield (Su)

A spelljack slowly develops an aura around themselves that disrupts the magic of others. At 4th level and every four levels thereafter, spelljack gains a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws against spells and spell-like abilities to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. The bonus to AC applies when flat-footed and to their touch AC.

Absorb Magic (Su)

Beginning at 6th level, a spelljack has learned to internalize magic meant to harm them. To do so, the spelljack must be the only target of a spell or spell-like ability and succeed on the saving throw against the effect; if they do, rather than being affected by the spell it is stolen as though by their steal magic ability.

Arcane Sight (Sp)

At 9th level the spelljack may cast arcane sight at will rather than detect magic.

Reflect Spell (Su)

Beginning at 11th level, a spelljack has learned to manipulate magical energy pointed directed at them and make that power their own. To do so, the spelljack must be the only target of a spell or spell-like ability and either succeed on the saving throw against the effect or the effect required an attack roll and missed the spelljack. The caster must immediately make a caster level check (DC 11 + the spelljack’s HD) or the spell effect is redirected back to the caster with the same attack roll and/or save DC. At 18th level, calculate the save DC as though it were cast by the spelljack instead and use either the new save DC or the original, whichever is greater. The spelljack may also roll a new attack roll for the spell as though they had cast it if it required an attack roll. If a spell qualifies for both absorb spell or reflect spell, only one may be used against the one particular spell.

Suppress Resistance (Su)

At 15th level, whenever the spelljack deals sneak attack damage to a creature with spell resistance, that creature loses an amount of spell resistance equal to 1/2 the spelljack’s caster level + the spelljack’s Intelligence modifier. This reduction lasts for one minute.

Additional attacks increase the duration but do not further reduce spell resistance.

Immediate Spell Release (Su)

At 18th level, when successfully stealing a spell from a target using the steal magic ability, the spelljack may choose to cast the spell as a free action in the round that the spell is initially stolen. Otherwise, the spell may be stored as normal. This ability is only usable on spells that use swift or standard actions to cast.

Spell Absorption Field (Su)

At 20th level, a spelljack gains the ability to augment and extend several of their class features into a 15 ft aura around themselves. Extending or ending this aura is a swift action. All allies including the spelljack in this radius benefit from the spell shield, absorb spell, and reflect spell abilities of the spelljack. This ability also now allows the spelljack to absorb and reflect area-of-effect spells and spell-like abilities rather than only those which target the spelljack. To do so when the spelljack (or any allies within 15 ft. of the spelljack) would be subject to a spell or spell-like ability which allows a saving throw and any of the affected allies or the spelljack succeed at their saving throw the spell is either absorbed by the spelljack or reflected, chosen by the spelljack. For area of effect spells which are reflected the spelljack chooses the new area as though the spelljack cast the original spell.

Alternate Capstone
Spell Void (Su)

At 20th level, a spelljack gains the ability to augment their spell shield, extending it into an aura that disrupts all spell casting within 10 ft. of the spelljack. By expending a 6th level spell slot as a standard action, a spelljack may project an aura that functions as an antimagic field except it doesn’t affect the spelljack and is centered on their square, following them if they move. This ability lasts for 6 rounds. At the beginning of each of the spelljack’s turns they may expend one of their prepared spells of the highest level they have available, or a stolen spell of level 6 or greater, if they do the spelljack may exclude a number of allies equal to the expended spell’s level minus 5 from the effect of spell void until the spelljack’s next turn.
